mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of declining FEDFUNDS instances or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of UNRATE > 5.0% instances or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in residential investment (HOUST) and rising consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals housing demand contraction and cost pressures that depress corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of HOUST decline/CPIAUCSL rise instances or interaction Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of declining industrial production (INDPRO) and rising consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), supply chain bottlenecks intensify cost pressures that reduce corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of INDPRO decline/CPIAUCSL rise instances or interaction Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of FEDFUNDS > 4.5% instances or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) consistently indicates labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of PAYEMS increase instances or Rank IC < 0.02 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of strong consumer demand (RSAFS > 350,000 million dollars) and high residential construction (HOUST > 2000 thousand units), robust economic activity supports corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: strong consumer and housing demand regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of RSAFS > 350k/HOUST > 2000 instances or interaction Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals stagflationary pressures that reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of CPIAUCSL rise/INDPRO decline instances or interaction Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.
